GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on

 MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

Project  Overview

The property  is located  within  the Rayo Industrial  (Sub-area  2) District  as shown  in the Community

designated  M3 and the rear portion  designated  IF.

*  Assessor's  Parcel  Numbers:  6222-005-028  and 6222-005-030

  Gate, Inc., FUBAR  Properties  LLC.

*  General  Plan Designation:  Rayo Industrial  District  (Sub-area  2)

*  Industrial  Flex (IF) and Heavy  Manufacturing  (M3)

*  Site Characteristics:  The subject  site measures  approximately  99,856  square feet (2.29 acres) and
  comprises  one irregular-shaped  parcel  having  primary  frontage  along  Rayo  Avenue.  A metal
  building,  approximately  12,550  square  feet, remains  on the southern  portion  of the site, along
  with  a storage  area, restrooms,  and other  spaces inside  the building.  The natural  grade  slopes
  towards  the southeastern  portion  of the site. The site is partially  paved  and fully  fenced.  There
  was an approximately  10-foot-tall  solid  metal  fence that spanned  along the easterly  frontage  of
  the site, which  has been removed  and replaced  with  a split-face  block  wall.  The project  site is
  accessed from  two driveway  aprons  on Rayo Avenue.

*  Surroundings:  Surrounding  properties  include  commercial  and industrial  uses to the north,  east,
  and west,  and a Los Angeles  Unified  School  District  (LAUSD)  facility  to the south.  A surface
  level  parking  lot is currently  being  developed  directly  to the north  and west of the subject  site
  and is intended  for an Amazon  parcel  delivery  vehicle  operation.  A metal recycling  facility  (ELG
  Metals  West  Coast  Inc.)  is located  to the  east  across  Rayo  Avenue.  LAUSD  operates  a
  maintenance  yard,  administrative  office,  and adult  school  to the south.

Project  Description

The project  consists  of an Ordinance,  amending  the citywide  Zoning  Map  of Title  11 (Zoning)  of
the South Gate Municipal  Code ("SGMC"),  to change  the zoning  designation  of the rear portion  of
the property  at 9313 Rayo Avenue  from  IF (Industrial  Flex)  to M3 (Heavy  Manufacturing),  to match
the current  M3 zoning  designation  of the front portion  of the property.  The property  is located  within
the Rayo Industrial  (Sub-area  2) District  as shown  in the Community  Design  Element  of the General
Plan.

Site improvements  were made over the past year to remove  an unpermitted  fence and replace  it with
a conforming  split-face  block  wall.  The applicant  plans to make  several  other  improvements  if the
Zone  Change  is approved  by the City  Council,  including  installation  of a new vehicle  storage  area

History  of Land  Use and Zoning  of Subject  Property

From  1941 to 1992, the site was occupied  by the Cooper  Drum  Company,  which  reconditioned  steel
drums  containing  industrial  chemicals.  The  property  remained  vacant  for  many  years  due  to
contamination  and has been deemed  a Superfund  site by the United  States Environmental  Protection
Agency  (EPA).  Throughout  the years, the site has been partially  treated  with  the installation  of test
wells  and extraction  of some chemicals.  EPA has continued  to oversee  cleanup  operations  conducted
by the prior  and current  property  owners.  Due to the site's  contamination,  EPA  imposed  certain
limitations  in conducting  site improvements  and type  of land uses/activities  permitted  within  the
site.  The  EPA  restrictions  in  combination  with  the  City's  Zoning  Code  have  limited  the
uses/activities  and improvements  that may be permitted  within  the subject  site.

In 2013, the property  lot lines were adjusted  to create the current  lot configuration  consisting  of two
Assessor  parcel  numbers.  Although  it consists  of two  parcel  numbers,  the site is identified  as one
legal parcel.  At the time,  the entire  property's  zoning  designation  was "M3"  (light  manufacturing).
Subsequently,  the  Zoning  Code  was  comprehensively  updated  in  2015,  which  resulted  in
amendments  to the Zoning  Map.  As part  of the update,  an "IF"  zoning  district  was introduced;
however,  it was not aligned  with  the property  lines of the subject  site. As a result,  the property  was
divided  into two zones: the landlocked  westerly  portion  designated  IF, and the easterly  portion  zoned
M3.

On December  19, 2024, the City  issued a Temporary  Certificate  of Occupancy  (TCO),  allowing  the
applicant  to operate  a vehicle  towing/impounding  lot only  within  the front  (easterly)  portion  of the
subject  site currently  designated  M3.  The  TCO  was issued  with  the understanding  the applicant
would  submit  a site plan for review  and approval  by staff  soon after.  The TCO  was subsequently
extended  while  the  Zone  Change  application  was  being  processed.  Pursuant  to Table  11.21-4
(Commercial  Industrial  Zones  Allowed  Land  Uses)  of  SGMC  Section  11.21.030  (Land  Use
Permission  Tables),  "vehicle  towing/impounding"  uses are permitted  by-right.  The  applicant  is

 DISCUSSION/ANALYSIS:

 Zoning  Map  Amendment
 The applicant  is requesting  to change  the zoning  of the rear portion  of the property  from  IF to M3,
to match  the current  M3 zoning  designation  of the front  portion  of the property,  with  the intention
to expand  the current  vehicle  towing  and impound  operations  to the remainder  of the site. If a zone
 change  is approved,  a separate  application  for Design  Review  will  be required  prior  to the approval
 and completion  of any site improvements  necessary  to accommodate  the business  expansion.  The
Design  Review  process  must be completed  before  the issuance  of a business  license  or Certificate
 of Occupancy  for the expanded  operations.  Design  Review  is an administrative  (staff  level)  process
that does not require  a public  hearing.

Pursuant  to SGMC  Section  11.22.060,  the purpose  of the IF zone is to continue  the industrial  job
base in the area, while  allowing  flexibility  to incorporate  a mix of uses and job options,  supporting
iru'iovative  industry  and living  options  in close proximity  to transit,  existing  employment  centers,
and  major  corridors.  Furthermore,  pursuant  to  SGMC  Section  11.24.060,  light  and  heavy
manufacturing  (M2  and M3)  zones are intended  to implement  the manufacturing/distribution  place
type designation  of the General  Plan. These  zones include  uses such as industrial,  manufacturing,
large-scale  warehouse,  distribution,  or logistics  facilities.  The M3 zone provides  dedicated  locations
for the preservation  and development  of commercial  and industrial  activities.

Properties  along  Rayo  Avenue,  between  Firestone  Boulevard  and Southern  Avenue,  are currently
designated  M3 and predominantly  occupied  by industrial  uses, with  the exception  of the LAUSD
facility  to the south of the project  site at 5115 Southern  Avenue,  which  is designated  IF. The front
portion  of the subject  site, which  abuts  Rayo  Avenue,  is also designated  M3,  aligning  with  the
zoning  of most properties  along  the street.  Therefore,  maintaining  this M3  zoning  designation  is
appropriate  to ensure  continued  compatibility  with  existing  and future  industrial  uses on adjacent
properties.  The  rear  portion  of the  site is designated  IF and shares  boundaries  with  other  IF-
designated  parcels  that front  Atlantic  Avenue.  The proposed  zone change  for the rear portion  of the
site supports  this zoning  pattern  and reinforces  consistency  along  Atlantic  Avenue.  Furthermore,
the change  would  facilitate  future  development  that aligns  with  surrounding  uses.

Environmental  Review
The proposed  Zone Change  constitutes  a "project"  under  the California  Environmental  Quality  Act
(CEQA).  The City  of South  Gate is the Lead Agency,  and an Initial  Study  (IS) was prepared  by
EcoTierra  Consulting,  Inc. in July 2026 to determine  whether  the Zone  Change  and the related  site
improvements  could  result in significant  effects  on the environment.  The Initial  Study  evaluated  all
twenty  CEQA  environmental  topic  areas, including  aesthetics,  air quality,  biological  and cultural
resources,  energy,  geology  and soils,  greenhouse  gas emissions,  hazards  and hazardous  materials,
hydrology  and water  quality,  land use and planning,  noise,  public  services,  transportation,  tribal
cultural  resources,  utilities,  and wildfire  (Attachment  C).

The analysis  considered  not only the map amendment  itself  but also the physical  improvements  the
applicant  proposes  if the Zone  Change  is approved  -  paving  and striping  of a new vehicle  storage
area, new  site lighting,  and construction  of an approximately  560-square-foot  office  building  -
along  with  approximately  52 cubic  yards  of soil cut, all of which  would  be exported,  and roughly
eight months  of construction  activity  beginning  in the first  quarter  of 2027.

Basis for Environmental  Concern.
As  described  in  the  Background  section  above,  the  site  was  used  for  drum  recycling  and
reconditioning  operations  from  the 1940s  until  2003  and has been  listed  by the United  States
Environmental  ProtectionAgency  (EPA)  on the Superfund  National  Priorities  List. Known  soil and
groundwater  contamination  remains,  and EPA continues  to oversee  cleanup  activities  at the site.
The Initial  Study  therefore  focused  on whether  ground-disturbing  activities  associated  with  the
proposed  site improvements  could  expose  workers,  the public,  or the environment  to hazardous
materials,  or degrade  water  quality.

Findings.
The Initial  Study  determined  that the project  would  result  in no impact  or a less-than-significant
impact  in all environmental  topic  areas except  Hazards  and Hazardous  Materials  and Hydrology
and Water  Quality,  which  were found  to be potentially  significant  unless  mitigated.  Because  these
two  areas could  be reduced  to a less-than-significant  level  through  mitigation,  the corresponding
Mandatory  Findings  of  Significance  were  likewise  identified  as potentially  significant  unless
mitigated.  No mitigation  was required  in any other topic  area.

Mitigation  Measure.
One mitigation  measure  was identified,  which  addresses  both areas of potential  impact:

  *  MM-HAZ-1  : Prior  to commencement  of any on-site  grading,  a Focused  Soil Management
  Plan ("SMP")  shall be approved  in accordance  with  the requirements  of the Department  of
  Toxic  Substances  Control  (DTSC),  U.S.  EPA,  the South  Coast Air  Quality  Management
  District  (SCAQMD),  and  the  Los  Angeles  Regional  Water  Quality  Control  Board
  (LARWQCB).  The SMP shall establish  procedures  for managing  soil disturbance  activities
  associated  with  the proposed  site improvements  based on existing  soil data, and shall define
  protocols  for addressing  previously  unknown  soil impacts  encountered  during  construction.
  The  SMP  shall  provide  guidance  for work  in areas of known  contamination  and outline
  contingency  measures  if previously  unidentified  hazardous  materials  or subsurface  features
  (such as underground  storage  tanks,  sumps,  clarifiers,  or septic tanks)  are encountered.  The
  SMP  shall  also  address  soil  management,  movement,  temporary  storage,  and disposal
  associated  with  site improvement  activities.

Conclusion  of Environmental  Review.
With  incorporation  of MM-HAZ-1,  all potentially  significant  impacts  would  be reduced  to less-
than-significant  levels.  Accordingly,  a Mitigated  Negative  Declaration  (MND)  was prepared  rather
than an Environmental  Impact  Report,  consistent  with  Section  15070  ofthe  State CEQA  Guidelines.

meal program  at the Senior  Center  in conjunction  with  the County  since 2004.  Prior to the signing
